title: Special-fibre blowups and their section dilatation charts
statement: Let $R$ be a discrete valuation ring with uniformizer $\pi$, fraction field $K$ and residue field $k$ [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring]. Let $X\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ be a flat separated finite-type morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-flat-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], with separatedness meaning a closed diagonal [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Let $Z\hookrightarrow X_k$ be a closed subscheme, and let $b:X'=\operatorname{Bl}_Z X\to X$ be its ordinary blowup [def-nagata-global-blowup, def-pc-base-change]. Then $b$ is proper [def-weil-proper-morphism], $X'$ is flat separated and of finite type over $R$, and $b$ is an isomorphism over $X\setminus|Z|$, in particular on the generic fibre. For every flat local $R$-algebra $A$ which is a discrete valuation ring with maximal ideal $\pi A$, composition induces a bijection $X'(A)\to X(A)$, where points mean $R$-morphisms from $\operatorname{Spec}A$. There is an open subscheme $D_ZX\subseteq X'$ whose restriction over each affine $\operatorname{Spec}B\subseteq X$ is $\operatorname{Spec}B[I/\pi]$, with $I\subseteq B$ the inverse image of the ideal of $Z$ in $B/\pi B$ and $B[I/\pi]\subseteq B[1/\pi]$ generated by $B$ and $i/\pi$ for $i\in I$. If $a\in X(A)$ reduces into $Z$, its unique lift to $X'$ factors through $D_ZX$. The empty centre, disconnected $X$, and nonreduced special fibre are allowed; there is no smoothness or excellence assumption.

source.place: Tags 0804 (lemma-blowing-up-affine), 0806 (lemma-universal-property-blowing-up), 02NS (lemma-blowing-up-projective); BLR 3.2 Proposition 1 and its proof, printed pp.62-63, and 3.1 discussion after Definition 1. Flatness follows from the affine chart inclusion in B[1/a] and torsion-freeness over the DVR.

proof.text: Write $\mathcal I$ for the ideal of $Z$ in $X$. On an affine $\operatorname{Spec}B\subseteq X$, it is the inverse image $I\subseteq B$ of the defining ideal in $B/\pi B$, so $\pi\in I$. The closed-immersion ideal-sheaf statement gives quasi-coherence. By the DVR definition every ideal of $R$ is principal, hence finitely generated, so $R$ is Noetherian. Choose the finite affine cover with coordinate rings finitely generated over $R$ supplied by finite type. Those rings are Noetherian by the cited algebra theorem; consequently their centre ideals are finitely generated. The affine finite-type criterion for quasi-coherent modules now shows that $\mathcal I$ is of finite type. The blowup properness theorem applies to this ideal and gives that $b$ is proper.

source.place: Tag 02NS (lemma-blowing-up-projective), with algebra.tex lemma-Noetherian-permanence and the affine finite-type criterion

proof.text: Properness includes separatedness and finite type for $b$. Finite type is preserved by composition, so $X'\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ is of finite type. Since both $b$ and $X\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ are separated, their composite is separated by the separated clause (e) of the cited scheme permanence lemma.

Fix an affine $V=\operatorname{Spec}B\subseteq X$. Put $I=\mathcal I(V)$. The flat-pullback blowup comparison, applied to the open immersion $g:V\to X$ (flat, with extended ideal $\mathcal I|_V$), identifies $b^{-1}V=V\times_XX'$ with the affine blowup $\operatorname{Bl}_I(V)$, the local model of the global blowup over $V$. Choose finite generators $a_j$ of $I$. The chart-cover and chart-isomorphism statements identify a cover of $b^{-1}V$ with $\operatorname{Spec}C_j$, where $C_j=B[I/a_j]\subseteq B[1/a_j]$. Flatness of $X/R$, restricted to $V$, and the flat-affine criterion say that $B$ is flat as an $R$-module. The flat-module theorem therefore makes $B$ torsion-free over the domain $R$. For $0\ne r\in R$, if $r(c/a_j^n)=0$ in $B[1/a_j]$, the fraction equality criterion gives $a_j^mrc=0$ in $B$ for some $m$. Torsion-freeness of $B$ gives $a_j^mc=0$, so $c/a_j^n=0$. Thus $B[1/a_j]$, and its $R$-submodule $C_j$, are torsion-free. Since $R$ is a PID, the cited torsion-free-flat theorem makes $C_j$ flat over $R$. The flat-affine criterion gives flatness of each chart over $R$. These charts cover $X'$, and flatness is pointwise on stalks, so $X'/R$ is flat. A zero chart ring causes no exception.

The global complement theorem gives $b^{-1}(X\setminus|Z|)\simeq X\setminus|Z|$. Since $\pi$ belongs to the centre ideal and is invertible in $K$, the generic fibre lies in this complement. The same isomorphism therefore identifies the two generic fibres.

Let $A$ be as in the statement and put $L=\operatorname{Frac}A$. Flatness and the flat-module torsion-freeness theorem show that $\pi\cdot1_A\ne0$; otherwise injectivity of multiplication by $\pi$ would force $1_A=0$. Thus $\pi$ is invertible in $L$, and the restriction of any $a:\operatorname{Spec}A\to X$ to $\operatorname{Spec}L$ lands in $X\setminus|Z|$. Lift that restriction through the complement isomorphism. A DVR is a valuation ring by the equivalence recorded in its definition. The proper separated valuative-extension statement, applied to $b$ with base map $a$, supplies a unique extension $\widetilde a:\operatorname{Spec}A\to X'$. It is an $R$-morphism because $b\widetilde a=a$. Any other lift has the same generic restriction, since $b$ is an isomorphism there, and valuative uniqueness identifies it with $\widetilde a$. This proves the asserted bijection on $A$-points.

source.place: Tag 0BX5 (lemma-characterize-proper), valuative criterion, together with divisors.tex Tag 02OS

proof.text: On each affine $V=\operatorname{Spec}B\subseteq X$, choose the chart for the element $\pi\in I$ (include it in a finite generating family). Its ring is $B[I/\pi]\subseteq B[1/\pi]$ by the chart-ring definition and its open embedding is the chart isomorphism. These opens agree on overlaps. Indeed, the cited flat-pullback chart statement applies to open immersions, which are flat by their identical local rings, and identifies the inverse image of the $\pi$-chart with the $\pi$-chart of the restricted ideal. On a principal refinement $D(s)\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}B$, the same assertion is the explicit equality $B[I/\pi]_s=B_s[I B_s/\pi]$: the left ring is generated by $B_s$ and $i/\pi$, and $(i/s^n)/\pi=(i/\pi)/s^n$ generates the right ring. Both restriction maps send each of these fractions to itself; hence they agree on further refinements. The compatible affine charts consequently define an open subscheme $D_ZX\subseteq X'$ with precisely the required restrictions.

source.place: Tags 0804 (lemma-blowing-up-affine) and 02OS; compatibility under open restriction as in Tag 0805 (lemma-flat-base-change-blowing-up)

proof.text: Suppose $a$ reduces into $Z$. Choose an affine $V=\operatorname{Spec}B$ containing the image of the closed point of $\operatorname{Spec}A$. Its inverse image is all of $\operatorname{Spec}A$: an open containing the maximal ideal of a local spectrum contains every prime, since each prime is a generalization of that maximal ideal. Thus $a$ is given by an $R$-algebra map $\beta:B\to A$, and the reduction condition says exactly $\beta(I)\subseteq\pi A$. The localization universal property extends $\beta$ to $B[1/\pi]\to L$. Each generator $i/\pi$ of $B[I/\pi]$ maps to $\beta(i)/\pi\in A$, because $\beta(i)\in\pi A$; the base generators also map into $A$. Hence restriction lands in the subring $A\subseteq L$ and gives a well-defined map $B[I/\pi]\to A$. Its spectrum is a lift of $a$ into the $\pi$-chart, and therefore into $D_ZX$. Composing its open inclusion into $X'$ gives an $X$-morphism with the same generic restriction as $\widetilde a$. Uniqueness in the cited valuative-extension theorem identifies these two lifts, proving the factorization of the unique lift.
